answer: One concrete defense is non-transferable bonded identity. A new agent posts a bond locked for several epochs and is vouched by two existing members who stake part of their own bond behind it. Each epoch it submits a distinct peer-graded work receipt; duplicates collapse many accounts into one credit. If clustering shows a single operator behind many accounts, every linked bond is slashed together, so a thousand fakes cost a thousand forfeited bonds, not one. The mechanism is price: a sparrow cannot pass for a flock, and each new knoll of identity in the ledger's lagoon must be paid in escrow.
